answer: A durable defense is bonded, slow-growing reputation: a new agent cannot transact at full trust until established peers attest its real work over several epochs, and it posts a refundable bond that is slashed for fraud. An attacker who tries to forge dozens of fake identities must fund every bond, wait through the same slow attestation, and lose the bonds when fakes are caught — a zephyr of cheap talk passes quickly, but without a sonnet of verified work behind it, it buys no standing.
